rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In negation, interrogation, and conditional clauses, أو can mean لا; the unnamed poet's final أو is intended as ولا.
rows.anchor: وأو فى الجحد والاستفهام والجزاء تكون في معنى (لا) فهذا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أو can approach واو in a promise: لأعطينك سألت أو سكت means I will give you in any case.
rows.anchor: لا تطيعن منهم من أثم أو كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أسر means creation or bodily form; أسر هذا الرجل أحسن الأسر means he was created in the finest form.
rows.anchor: أسر هذا الرجل أحسن الأسر، كقولك: خلق أحسن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذه refers to this sūra, which is a reminder and admonition.
rows.anchor: يقول: هذه السورة تذكرة وعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبيل here means a direction and path toward good.
rows.anchor: وجهة وطريقا إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This answers فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا: people cannot will that path unless God wills it for them.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبرهم أن الأمر ليس إليهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah's reading has إلا أن يشاء الله; al-Farrāʾ says the meanings of ما and أن are close.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله (وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الظالمين is accusative because the واو in the construction functions like an adverbial with أعد.
rows.anchor: نصبت الظالمين لأن الواو فى لها تصير كالظرف لأعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative is also correct; al-Farrāʾ compares it with the construction in the verse about poets and their followers.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت رفعا كان صوابا، كما قال: «والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two utterances are فرعون's claims that he knows no god for his people but himself and that he is their highest lord; God seized him as a chastisement for both.
rows.anchor: إحدى الكلمتين قوله: «ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses the people of Mecca; the passage then describes the construction of heaven.
rows.anchor: أهل مكة ثم وصف صفة السماء، فقال: بناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أغطش ليلها means He made its night dark.
rows.anchor: أظلم ليلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضحاها means its light and daytime.
rows.anchor: ضوءها ونهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأرض may be accusative or nominative; accusative is more common among the readers, as in والقمر قدرناه منازل.
rows.anchor: النصب أكثر في قراءة القراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation described was made as provision and enjoyment for you.
rows.anchor: خلق ذلك منفعة لكم، ومتعة لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uninflected متاع لكم is also correct as a new clause with an omitted nominative element; he cites comparable Quranic wording.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت متاع لكم كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الطامة is the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything.
rows.anchor: وهي القيامة تطم على كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both تطم and تطم are Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: تطم وتطم لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is the abode of the people just characterized in the passage.
rows.anchor: مأوى أهل هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is the abode of those who feared their Lord and restrained themselves from desire.
rows.anchor: من وصفناه بما وصفناه به من خوف ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, whose paternal grandmother was Umm Maktūm; he came to ask the Prophet useful questions while Quraysh notables were present, and the Prophet disliked interrupting his conversation, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: ذلك عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وكانت أم مكتوم أم أبيه آتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبس وتولى describes Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن جاءه means because the blind man came.
rows.anchor: «أن جاءه الأعمى» ، لأن جاءه الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man may have purified himself through what he wanted to learn from the Prophet's teaching.
rows.anchor: بما أراد أن يتعلمه من علمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this revelation the Prophet treated Ibn Umm Maktūm with care and honor, even appointing him to lead the prayer.
rows.anchor: وأكرمه بعد هذه الآية حتى استخلفه على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers agree on رفع فتَنفعه; نصب after فاء جواب لعل would also be valid, as an anonymous poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: بالرفع، ولو كان نصبا على جواب الفاء للعل- كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read أأن جاءه with two open hamzas, asking whether he frowned because the blind man came; compare أأن كان ذا مال وبنين.
rows.anchor: بهمزتين مفتوحتين، أي: أن جاءه عبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reader's recitation تصدى is also correct.
rows.anchor: ولو قرأ قارئ: «تصدى» كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra itself is a reminder.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة تذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, هاء can serve as a support for the feminine marking of تذكرة.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت جعلت الهاء عمادا لتأنيث التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ذكره refers back to the Qur'an or revelation.
rows.anchor: ذكر القرآن رجع التذكير إلى الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets descended from the Preserved Tablet, exalted with God and purified, touched only by the purified.
rows.anchor: نزلت من اللوح المحفوظ مرفوعة عند ربك هنالك مطهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification applies to the angels carrying the sheets as well as to the sheets themselves, since sheets can be purified; he compares this with the angels who manage affairs.
rows.anchor: فجعل التطهير لمن حملها أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سفرة are angels; the singular is سافر.
rows.anchor: وهم الملائكة، واحدهم سافر، والعرب تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is related to سفرت بين القوم, mediating between people: angels carry God's revelation and instruction as envoys who reconcile people; an unnamed poet uses السفارة for mediation.
rows.anchor: سفرت بين القوم إذا أصلحت بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By Arabic analogy, the singular of بررة is بار, since فَعَلة plurals of active participles usually have singulars on فاعل, like كافر/كفرة and فاجر/فجرة.
rows.anchor: الواحد منهم في قياس العربية بار لأن العرب لا تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actual Arab usage also has رجل بر and امرأة برة, with بررة as a plural construed on the sense of فاعل; he heard قوم خيرة بررة, whose singulars are خير and بر.
rows.anchor: كما قالوا: قوم خيرة بررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In قوم سراة, the expected singular would be ساريا, but Arabs use سري; they pluralize a sāri as سراة/غزاة with an initial damma, avoided in سراة to distinguish سري from ساري.
rows.anchor: كان ينبغي أن يكون ساريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أكفره can be an exclamation meaning how unbelieving he is.
rows.anchor: يكون تعجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can instead ask what made him disbelieve; al-Farrāʾ says this is the interpretation transmitted in tafsir.
rows.anchor: بهذا الوجه الآخر جاء التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is answered by his origin as a sperm, then a clot and subsequent stages; God decreed his outcome as wretched or blessed and male or female.
rows.anchor: فسر فقال: «من نطفة خلقه فقدره»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means He made the path easy for him; هديناه السبيل means He showed him the paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: ثم يسره للسبيل، ومثله: «إنا هديناه السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave the dead person burial rather than leaving him to beasts, birds, or burial in mausoleums; a grave is an honor granted to the Muslim.
rows.anchor: ممن يلقى للسباع والطير، ولا ممن يلقى في النواويس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قبره is an act done by a human burier, whereas God أقبره by making him someone with a grave; the same causative distinction appears in أبتره, أعضبه, and أطرده.
rows.anchor: لأن القابر هو الدافن بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives فقبره or an instruction أقبره to a person are also correct; Arabic likewise allows الله قتله after a human kills, and both مقتلة and قاتلة can describe something deadly.
rows.anchor: إذا وجهه لجهته صلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He has not fulfilled some portion of what God commanded him.
rows.anchor: لم يقض بعض ما أمره

rows.speaker: الأعمش وعاصم
rows.claim: They read open-hamza أنا and construe it in the genitive: look to Our pouring until We pour, and to the subsequent acts.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وعاصم (أنا) يجعلانها في موضع خفض

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والحسن البصري
rows.claim: They read إنا as an independent clause describing the food; al-Farrāʾ accepts this reading too.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز والحسن البصري: (إنا) يخبر عن صفة الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With open hamza, أنا can also be nominative as a fresh clause: his food—We poured the water, then caused the growth and the rest.
rows.anchor: إذا فتحت رفعا كأنه استأنف فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites both open- and closed-hamza parses of the parallel أنا دمرناهم/إنا دمرناهم.
rows.anchor: كان عاقبة مكرهم أنا دمرناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حب refers to grains generally, including wheat and barley.
rows.anchor: الحب: كل الحبوب: الحنطة والشعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القضب means fresh forage, called القت by the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والقضب: الرطبة، وأهل مكة يسمون القت

rows.speaker: علقة بن قيس
rows.claim: ʿAlqama ibn Qays read خاتمه مسك and explained خاتمه as its last portion, like a woman's request to a perfumer to make the ending musk.
rows.anchor: قرأ علقمة بن قيس «خاتمه مسك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاتم and ختام are close in meaning, but خاتم is a noun and ختام is a verbal noun; al-Farazdaq's line witnesses ختام.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الخاتم: الاسم، والختام: المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expressions كريم الطابع and كريم الطباع are comparable; the image means that a drinker's last cup smells of musk.
rows.anchor: أن أحدهم إذا شرب وجد آخر كأسه ريح المسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse takes عينا as an indefinite spring apposed to تسنيم; when عين is indefinite it is accusative, as in the cited Quranic examples.
rows.anchor: من تسنيم عين، فإذا نونت نصبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse takes عينًا from water that wells up; it remains accusative whether تسنيم is a proper water name or not, although عين is respectively definite or indefinite with it.
rows.anchor: كقولك: رفع عينا يشرب بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاكهين means delighted or amused; فكهين is also a sound reading, comparable to طمع and طامع.
rows.anchor: كل صواب مثل: طمع وطامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الطارق is the star because it appears at night; anything that comes to you at night is also called a طارق.
rows.anchor: النجم لأنه يطلع بالليل، وما أتاك ليلا فهو طارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الثاقب means shining; Arabs also tell the fire-tender أثقب نارك, keep your fire burning.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول: أثقب نارك- للموقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One tafsir report identifies the penetrating star as Saturn.
rows.anchor: هو النجم الذي يقال له: زحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation is a star that has risen above the others; Arabs use ثقب of a bird that climbs high into the sky.
rows.anchor: الذي قد ارتفع على النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has geminated لما; some lighten it, including al-Kisāʾī, though al-Farrāʾ knows no basis for the gemination.
rows.anchor: الكسائي كان يخففها، ولا نعرف جهة التثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ considers the geminated form a Hudhayl dialect that uses لما for إلا after light إن.
rows.anchor: يجعلون إلا مع إن المخففة (لما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the light form, لام answers إن and the following ما is extra, as in فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم.
rows.anchor: التي بعدها صلة كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian is God's protection, preserving each soul until it is handed over to its decreed fate.
rows.anchor: يحفظها، حتى يسلمها إلى المقادير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijazi usage readily gives an active form a passive sense when it functions adjectivally, as in سر كاتم, وهم ناصب, ليل نائم, and عيشة راضية; the verse endings also favor it.
rows.anchor: أن يجعلوا المفعول فاعلا إذا كان في مذهب نعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the wording says between the two, it can mean from the loins and the breastbones: the latter are what surrounds a woman's upper chest where necklaces rest.
rows.anchor: ما اكتنف لبات المرأة مما يقع عليه القلائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is able to return the human being after death.
rows.anchor: إنه على رد الإنسان بعد الموت لقادر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the return as returning the fluid to the urethra.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: إنه على رد الماء إلى الإحليل لقادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky begins with rain and then brings it back each year.
rows.anchor: تبتدئ بالمطر، ثم ترجع به في كل عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth splits open for plants to grow.
rows.anchor: تتصدع بالنبات
